proposals.title: Evaluate inlining the existing compiled homepage stylesheet
proposals.hypothesis: Inlining the unchanged compiled stylesheet at its existing homepage cascade position may remove one render-blocking request. This is a performance hypothesis, not a proven speed improvement. Preserve all content, contact destinations, CSP and other page output; keep the shared CSS asset for other routes.
proposals.measurementPlan: Before launch, the existing central owner must review the baseline and exact homepage-only treatment, accept the plan, resolve baseline gaps and enroll its genuine experiment ID through the existing receipt process. Compare retained eligible mobile evidence on comparable collection conditions after a separately approved release, separating deterministic request removal from noisy FCP/LCP or score movement. Local checks establish exact CSS bytes, original HTML restoration, unchanged other files, contact guards and transfer-size tradeoffs. No new scan, collector, cadence or provider call is requested by this proposal. Inconclusive speed evidence remains inconclusive. Any rollback requires its own applicable delivery authority.
baselineGaps: Retained mobile observation is 19 October 2026, not a fresh controlled prelaunch timing baseline.
Removing one stylesheet request does not establish lower FCP/LCP or a higher performance score.
Local gzip HTML plus CSS is 32500 bytes before versus 33107 bytes after; cache and repeat-view effects are unmeasured.
Central plan acceptance, baseline disposition and exact experiment collector enrollment have not been supplied.
